videos.title: Weekly AI Recap: GrokBot Just Did the Unthinkable, ChatGPT Looks Completely Different & More!
videos.ai_tech_id: xAI Grok Bot, Anthropic Claude/Claude Cowork, Midjourney, Suno, OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini/Nano Banana 2.1
summary: Paul Lipsky runs his weekly AI news recap, leading with Grok Bot's plan to integrate Claude, Midjourney, and Suno into its automation stack, a move he frames as a notable expansion of what the bot can orchestrate across providers.

He covers OpenAI's rollout of a new "Intelligent UI" for ChatGPT that changes how the interface looks and behaves, Anthropic's move of Claude Cowork to the cloud, and Google updates including Gemini plan changes and the Nano Banana 2.1 image model, alongside a hands-on test of Google Playground.

The video is sponsored by Okou (an AI tool with a discount code for viewers) and closes with Paul's own takeaways on the week's developments, serving as a digest format for viewers tracking shifts across multiple major AI labs at once.

videos.title: Does Gemini's Write Like Me make emails sound like you?
summary: Futurepedia tests Gemini's new "Write Like Me" skill, which pulls writing samples from the user's sent email folder to learn their tone, sentence length, openings, and closings.

Once set up, the skill can be invoked in any new chat: the user pastes in an email and a short instruction like "decline this," and Gemini drafts a reply styled to match how that person actually writes, aiming for a one-click-ready response.

The video is pitched at people who let repetitive emails pile up, presenting the skill as a quick setup that pays off in reclaimed time, and fits Futurepedia's pattern of walking through a single practical AI feature in depth.

videos.title: The Ultimate Image Generator Showdown
videos.ai_tech_id: Nano Banana 2.1 vs. OpenAI ChatGPT Image 2.5, Flux 3 Image, and Seedream 5.0
summary: Prompted by the release of Nano Banana 2.1, Futurepedia runs a head-to-head comparison against ChatGPT Image 2.5, Flux 3 Image, and Seedream 5.0 across identical prompts.

The test spans marketing materials, image editing, infographics, photorealism, human character consistency, thumbnail generation, style transfer, and character sheets, with a winner declared for each category and an overall tally at the end.

The video functions as a practical buyer's guide for creators choosing an image-generation model for specific use cases rather than a single "best overall" pick, with chapter markers for each test category.

videos.title: Oracle's New AI Only Thinks When It Has To
videos.ai_tech_id: Oracle Fusion Claw — enterprise AI/agent orchestration tool
summary: Nate Herk covers Oracle's newly announced "Fusion Claw," an enterprise AI system pitched around the idea that it only invokes model reasoning when a task actually needs it, letting conventional software handle the rest.

The brief description frames this as a cost and efficiency play: rather than routing every action through an LLM, Fusion Claw reserves AI reasoning for the specific decision points where it adds value, with deterministic software covering the rest of the workflow.

The video ties into Oracle's AI World event in Las Vegas (Oct 26-27), where the product will be shown live, positioning this as an early look at enterprise-grade agentic tooling ahead of a bigger announcement.

videos.title: 10 Secret ChatGPT Codes to Learn Anything
videos.ai_tech_id: OpenAI ChatGPT — structured study/prompting technique codes
summary: Sabrina Ramonov shares 10 short prompt "codes" meant to turn ChatGPT into a more active study partner instead of a simple answer engine.

The codes include ELI5 and FEYNMAN-TECHNIQUE for simplified explanations, 80/20 for prioritizing high-value material, QUIZME and SOCRATES for active-recall and question-driven learning, and visual-output prompts like MAKE-STICKY-NOTES, MAKE-MINDMAP, MAKE-VISUAL-STUDYGUIDE, FIRSTPRINCIPLES, and MAKE-SCHEMATIC.

Viewers are told to start with one command and paste their topic (or notes) after it, giving a reusable prompt library aimed at students or anyone using ChatGPT to learn new material more efficiently than with ad-hoc questions.
